material.description: js/client/feedback.js:98-102 shows the refusal line in onEvent with no enabled() check. draw() hides it only on an on-to-off transition (wasOn, declared :53, tested at :194-196), and drawRefusal (:186-189) runs only from draw() at :204, which returns early while off. A refusal event that arrives with the layer off from the start (window.__fxOff=true or window.__mobaFeedback.enabled=false, read in enabled() at :114) leaves refusal display:block until the layer is re-enabled, past REFUSAL_MS (1.2 s). Principle: visibility of system status (Nielsen 1) and error recovery (Nielsen 9). Reachability: the switch is a debug flag; codeinsight callers of setEnabled show no call into the feedback layer (dispatch 1792858315891-4098-2d61598ff6a43203). Witness: codesearch literal 'refusal' on feedback.js (dispatch 1792858226287-3856-7a57ba02c105e42), 'wasOn' (1792858361263-4225-a341199babc676a8), 'if (!on)' (1792858361676-4228-8be9a52433ec7da0), 'drawRefusal(t)' (1792858362093-4230-5e5f243343b4eb66). Traced from code, not run live.
material.subject: Refusal line stays on screen while the feedback layer is switched off
material.witness: js/client/feedback.js:102 refusal returns when !enabled(); live eval at 94285ce0 with layer disabled from start: pre-fix sha a5f84d56 refusal display=block, fixed sha none; no stale show after re-enable; enabled refusal shows block (verify-dada_nielsen-trav-feedback-1). CI ci run 40112073190 success 3/3 (pages run superseded).
